## Hypotheses, challenges and experimental decisions

The investigation treats an explanation as a prediction about an intervention. The first 78 image fits were inspected before the hypotheses below were revised. The full 36-fit initialization cohort and the scratch-500 cohort had yet to be interpreted when this record was written. The synthetic scalar-ridge control is a challenger-designed diagnostic using the original five training blocks and fresh oracle inputs.

| Candidate explanation | Discriminating evidence | Resulting claim |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Different unrestricted mean targets explain the TailRL/mean-MSE gap | Complete-radius population optimization, CDF tangent proof, exact orbit and inverse-KKT checks | The implemented equal-radius population TailRL objective recovers the conditional mean on the full simplex. Restricted models and finite training supply the relevant remaining distinctions. |
| A scalar bottleneck explains the point-prediction advantage | Scalar versus categorical mean-MSE; fixed, affine and free residual heads | Categorical mean-MSE has lower selected error than scalar MSE in all six clean/noisy block comparisons. Scalar sharing has an approximation and optimization tradeoff. |
| MSE encoder supervision improves age information across label regimes | The full head-loss by encoder-loss routing factorial, followed by common readouts | Clean selected predictors favor the MSE encoder route with either head. Under SD-10, the route effect changes with the head objective. Common readouts locate the contribution accessible through the declared probe. |
| Full categorical freedom necessarily lowers point accuracy | Free versus affine residuals with matched starting functions, plus certified synthetic fits | CE benefits from the affine restriction in both image label regimes; noisy TailRL benefits relative to the affine control, while its clean comparisons differ. The synthetic cost of weak residual regularization falls with sample size and strong shrinkage. |
| Extra categorical freedom explains the small endpoint-law synthetic gain | Three validation candidates for scalar ridge, compared with the three retained flexible-head candidates | Scalar shrinkage substantially improves the smaller-sample endpoint estimator. The positive result concerns the declared regularization procedures and preserves the full model's ability to approach a scalar solution under suitable penalties. |
| The useful age structure acts through the initial function | Float32 ordinary categorical heads with binomial versus random initialization | Pending the complete matched initialization comparison. |
| A persistent, strongly loaded age coordinate improves optimization | Float32 fused versus scalar-plus-residual heads with the same starting function and full categorical family | Pending the complete matched initialization comparison; a normalized-score control is conditional on a material repeated clean-CE difference. |
| Long-horizon differences reflect different fitting trajectories | Repeated 500-epoch scratch fits, retained fixed epochs, common readouts and corruption-following slopes | Pending the repeated long-horizon cohort. |

### Prospective initialization predictions

The clean structured-CE improvement motivates a signed prediction: binomial initialization should improve an ordinary categorical CE head over random initialization when precision and coordinates match. Comparing the fused ordinal head with the redundant score-plus-residual head separates a starting-function contribution from a persistent-coordinate contribution. A starting-function explanation predicts that fused and redundant heads remain relatively close compared with their gap from the random head. A persistent-coordinate explanation predicts a further change after head updates even though the two initial functions agree.

The completed first cohort motivates an objective-by-time interaction for TailRL. Its structured free head selects later checkpoints under SD-10, and its selected and final comparisons have opposite signs. The initialization study should therefore report learning speed, selected accuracy and common final-epoch accuracy separately for each objective and label regime.

If a repeated, practically material clean-CE fused-versus-free difference remains, the challenger proposes a normalized persistent score. Let $a_c=a-49.5$, $N=\sqrt{83325}$ and $e=a_c/N$. Replacing $a\,s(h)$ by $e\,u(h)$ with $u(h)=Ns(h)$ at initialization preserves the initial policy up to a common logit shift. With a free residual, the attainable categorical family also agrees. For Euclidean head-only SGD, the age-coordinate contribution to the logit kernel changes from $a_ca_c^\top$ to $ee^\top$. Under Adam, the resulting intervention includes adaptive normalization and clipping. Moving the normalized head toward the fused trajectory would support the loading of the persistent age coordinate as a contributor. A remaining separation would motivate the broader redundant-coordinate or update-interaction explanation.

### Prospective long-horizon predictions

The retained earlier scratch results motivate three observations to check in the repeated cohort: scalar MAE should have a useful learning horizon extending beyond ordinary TailRL's selected epoch; continued TailRL optimization should improve its supplied-label objective during a period of worsening held-out point error; and opening free residual directions should change the amount or timing of that late fitting relative to the affine control.

Common readouts distinguish two outcomes. A remaining difference with the same ridge procedure identifies a change in age information accessible to that procedure. Recovery of the native-head gap by refitting identifies a contribution from the stored readout and its coadaptation with the encoder. Corruption-following slopes and age bands provide a further observation of fitting the particular supplied field. Agreement across these measurements supports the corresponding location of the effect.

The retained checkpoints and complete trajectories allow every prediction to be evaluated at its stated horizon. The final report will update this register with all completed outcomes, including revisions to the explanation.

### Challenger follow-up after the 36 initialization fits

The completed float32 cohort supports the clean CE starting-function prediction: the ordinary binomial-initialized head improves selected MAE by 0.653 years relative to the ordinary random head, with gains in all three blocks. The additional free-score path has a small average difference with mixed block signs. The conditional normalized-score experiment therefore stays outside the executed fit set. The early-closeness prediction is revised: fused and free coordinates produce large, reversing early differences despite similar endpoint averages.

The independent challenger sharpens the next question to the numerical assignment of that starting function. The proposed control swaps rows only within symmetric pairs $\{a,99-a\}$. Since $\log {99\choose a}=\log {99\choose99-a}$, these swaps preserve each age's base binomial coefficient. Whole-row permutation also preserves the initial probability multiset, entropy, head norm, rank and full attainable categorical family. Actual target labels and the ages used to evaluate the mean stay fixed.

The mapping is frozen without examining labels or outcomes: an isolated CPU generator uses seed $2026102937+\text{head\_seed}$ and chooses exactly 25 of the 50 symmetric pairs to swap. The same block mapping is used for clean and SD-10 fits. This gives six fits under the existing 50-epoch protocol. Clean CE is the primary comparison against the retained ordered and random ordinary heads; SD-10 is secondary.

Write $\pi$ for the involution and $\mu_F=\sum_a a p_F(a)$. The swapped starting function has $z_a^P=\log {99\choose a}+\pi(a)s$, hence

$$
\nabla_h L_{\mathrm{CE}}^{P}(x,y)
=w[\mu_F(x)-\pi(y)],
\qquad
\nabla_h L_{\mathrm{CE}}^{F}(x,y)
=w[\mu_F(x)-y].
$$

Both initial corrections share one feature direction, while the swapped correction uses the altered numerical code. The signed prediction is lower clean selected error for the ordered assignment. A repeated improvement would support coherent numerical assignment beyond the retained base coefficient, entropy and rank. Similar performance would redirect the explanation toward the broader starting-state package. The swaps retain distance from the midpoint, and changes in example weighting, correction sign and clipping remain part of the intervention. Its interpretation concerns the complete numerical-assignment change under the declared optimizer.
